body.translated_text: The <s>Vairāgyaśatakam</s> (Hundred Verses on Renunciation) composed by the illustrious <s>Appaya Dīkṣita</s>.

children.translated_text: There lives a certain mendicant (<s>bhikṣu</s>) who has mastered the ten indeclinables (<s>avyayas</s>);
the pair of indeclinables 'not' and 'mine' — we beg for that; what else is there? // <s>AppVs</s>_1 //
Having intellect (<s>dhī</s>) as minister, fortitude (<s>dhairya</s>) as strength, with resolve (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) as the opposing [army], and peace (<s>śānti</s>) as its treasury,
this <s>vairāgya</s> (renunciation) is a sovereignty whose domain is the three worlds. // <s>AppVs</s>_2 //

children.text: rājño bibheti loko rājānaḥ punarito 'pi vairibhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The world fears the king; kings in turn fear their enemies;
from [the creator] <s>Brahmā</s> [down to the lowest being, all fear] the god of death — but the kingdom of desirelessness (<s>aspṛhā</s>) is free from fear on every side. // <s>AppVs</s>_3 //

children.text: bhikṣāpradā jananyaḥ pitaro guravaḥ kumārakāḥ śiṣyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who give alms are [his] mothers; the elders are [his] fathers; young boys are [his] pupils;
peace (<s>śānti</s>) is the beloved who is the sole cause of delight for the renunciant. // <s>AppVs</s>_4 //
Those who do not exert themselves at all, due to the absence of both action and reaction —

children.text: santasta eva muktāḥ saṃdehe gautamaḥ sākṣī || 5 ||
children.translated_text: such saints are themselves liberated; in [this] matter of doubt, <s>Gautama</s> [the Buddha] is the witness. // <s>AppVs</s>_5 //

children.text: patatu nabhaḥ sphuṭatu mahī calantu girayo milantu vāridhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Let the sky fall, let the earth burst, let the mountains move, let the oceans unite —
let the world be turned upside down: what loss is there for one who is free from attachment? // <s>AppVs</s>_6 //

children.text: ke corāḥ ke piśunāha ke ripavaḥ ke 'pi dāyādāḥ /
children.translated_text: Who are the thieves? Who are the slanderers? Who are the enemies? Who are the rival heirs?

children.text: jagadakhilaṃ tasya vaśe yasya vaśe syādidaṃ cetaḥ || 7 ||
children.translated_text: The entire world is under the control of one whose own mind is under control. // <s>AppVs</s>_7 //
Let sense-objects present themselves, or let the senses rush toward the objects —

children.text: āntaramekaṃ karaṇaṃ śāntaṃ yadi kā tataścintā || 8 ||
children.translated_text: if the one inner faculty [the mind] is at peace, what worry is there then? // <s>AppVs</s>_8 //
Must the foolish dwell in the caves of <s>Meru</s> to avoid sense-objects?
Indeed, lotuses do not grow on mineral ores even when watered! // <s>AppVs</s>_9 //
In this disease of worldly existence (<s>bhava-roga</s>), ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) is the root cause, birth itself is the premonitory symptom,
transmigration (<s>saṃsāra</s>) is the full manifestation, and the ultimate peace (<s>naiṣṭhikī śānti</s>) is the remedy. // <s>AppVs</s>_10 //
Like a man who remembers his former birth as a pig, [recoiling from] the food he himself consumed [then],
the wise person, feeling disgust from afar, cherishes renunciation (<s>vairāgya</s>). // <s>AppVs</s>_11 //

children.text: śaiśavamiva kaumāre tattaruṇimnīva sa iva vṛddhatve /
children.translated_text: Just as childhood [delights] do not please in youth, and those of youth do not [please] in maturity, and those of maturity do not [please] in old age,

children.text: na svadate dhīrāṇāṃ kāmasya viceṣṭitaṃ śāntau || 12 ||
children.translated_text: so too the activities of desire do not please the wise in [the state of] peace. // <s>AppVs</s>_12 //
Having examined sense-objects a hundred times, [the wise] promptly abandon them here and there;
others, like crows eating vomited food, continue to indulge in those very [objects]. // <s>AppVs</s>_13 //
Mother and father depart at last; the wife departs at last; the sons depart at last —
even in love that must be given, how do the wise become dispassionate here? // <s>AppVs</s>_14 //
The fickle whirl about like straw when the fierce wind of women's names blows;
the saintly, like mountains, do not tremble in the slightest there. // <s>AppVs</s>_15 //
In the pleasure of desire — the supreme enjoyment of the lustful — the saints, who delight in the taste of tranquility,
feel revulsion, as do the gods who feed on nectar toward the food of pigs. // <s>AppVs</s>_16 //
Those whose knowledge has reached the stage of full expansion, being possessed of mere distraction [from the world],
observe even their own activities as though they were those of another. // <s>AppVs</s>_17 //
The wise follow fools who are fixated on the wrong things and content in the wrong places,

children.text: anuvartante dhīrāḥ pitara iva krīḍato bālān || 18 ||
children.translated_text: as parents [follow] children at play. // <s>AppVs</s>_18 //

children.text: puṣṇati puruṣe salilairmuṣṇati puṣpaṃ phalaṃ ca tarava iva /
children.translated_text: Just as trees, when a person waters them, rob [him of] both flowers and fruit,
so the saints behave alike toward those who help them and those who harm them. // <s>AppVs</s>_19 //
The discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal — for everyone it exists [merely] at the level of [distinguishing] a pot from a non-pot;
that discrimination which produces peace — any other [discrimination], however comprehensive, is non-discrimination. // <s>AppVs</s>_20 //

children.text: anadhigate kāmasukhe kālena yathā pravartate taruṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a youth, when the pleasure of desire was not yet experienced, naturally engages in it with time,
so too some fortunate one engages even in the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> [spontaneously, by good fortune]. // <s>AppVs</s>_21 //
The virtues of sons are to be seen [only] in [matters of] independence; the virtues of wives, on the occasion of remarriage;
the virtues of brothers, at the time of inheritance division — [these should be observed] by one about to be liberated. // <s>AppVs</s>_22 //

children.text: kā me gatiriti pṛcchati caramaśvāse 'pi yaḥ svārtham /
children.translated_text: Even at his final breath, one who asks 'What is my destiny?' [only] for his own [worldly] interest —

children.text: tasya janasyāpi kṛte pāpāḥ pāpāni kurvanti || 23 ||
children.translated_text: even for the sake of such a person, the sinful commit sins. // <s>AppVs</s>_23 //
They quarrel with [their] fathers, yet teach their sons filial devotion;
they take other men's wives, yet study the <s>śāstras</s> [on duty] to their own wives. // <s>AppVs</s>_24 //
Peace (<s>śānti</s>) is [called] unobtainable; cessation (<s>uparati</s>) is [called] unworthiness; the refusal of gifts is [called] disqualification;
patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) is [called] weakness — such are the [perverted views of] the dharmas of renunciation in the <s>Kali</s> age. // <s>AppVs</s>_25 //

children.text: nītijñā niyatijñā vedajñā api bhavanti śāstrajñāḥ /
children.translated_text: There are those who know statecraft, those who know fate, those who know the <s>Vedas</s>, and those who know the <s>śāstras</s>;
even knowers of <s>Brahman</s> may be found — but rare are those who know their own ignorance. // <s>AppVs</s>_26 //

children.text: kalikaluṣe manasi sve kathamiva jagadārjavaṃ labhate /
children.translated_text: When one's own mind is polluted by the <s>Kali</s> [age], how can one find straightforwardness in the world?
When a defect exists in the eye itself, how can the doubling of the moon go away? // <s>AppVs</s>_27 //
To make sense-objects agreeable, let effort be applied to the perceiver — the heart;

children.text: dṛśi deyamauṣadhaṃ ko dṛśye dattvā sukhī bhavati || 28 ||
children.translated_text: who becomes happy by applying medicine to the [external] object seen, when the medicine should be given to the eye [itself]? // <s>AppVs</s>_28 //
Wives are devoted to their sons; sons are busy seizing the father's wealth;
the mother takes refuge in weeping — who is the kinsman of one who has departed to the other world? // <s>AppVs</s>_29 //
They see those who are dying; they approve of those who are about to die; they remember the dead;
they speak in this [matter-of-fact] way — yet they behave as though they themselves were eternal. // <s>AppVs</s>_30 //

children.text: kalahāyante mūḍhāḥ kaḥ pratibhūḥ śvaḥ prabhāta iti /
children.translated_text: Fools quarrel [as if forever] — who guarantees that tomorrow's dawn will come?

children.text: tasyāmeva rajanyāṃ kaḥ pratibhūḥ svasya sattāyām || 31 ||
children.translated_text: On that very night, who guarantees one's own continued existence? // <s>AppVs</s>_31 //
They have dug broad canals, built walls bound with stones,

children.text: krītā balino mahipāḥ kṛtakṛtyāḥ sma iti manyante || 32 ||
children.translated_text: purchased powerful kings [as allies] — and think 'We have accomplished our purpose.' // <s>AppVs</s>_32 //

children.text: ā prapadamā śiraskaṃ cāntaḥ kalimalamalīmase vapuṣi /
children.translated_text: From head to toe, both inside and out, we are defiled with the impurity of the <s>Kali</s> [age] in our body;
even the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is as fruitless [for such a one] as a handful of <s>darbha</s> grass [thrown] into a pot of liquor. // <s>AppVs</s>_33 //

children.text: daṇḍyaṃ yatsukhahetoḥ puṣṇanti janāḥ kathaṃ tadeva vapuḥ /
children.translated_text: Why do people nourish this very body, which should be punished, for the sake of pleasure?
Indeed, those who desire sugar do not worship the stalks of sugarcane [themselves]. // <s>AppVs</s>_34 //
Generally, the mind of a living being becomes deluded at the moment of the departure of the vital breath;

children.text: puṇyena yadi na muhyati putrāneva smaranmriyate || 35 ||
children.translated_text: if by merit it is not deluded, [even then] one dies remembering only one's sons. // <s>AppVs</s>_35 //
To quench the fire of the belly, they plunge into the ocean called <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence);
to cure the distress of cold, one should not set fire to the house! // <s>AppVs</s>_36 //
Wealth, acquired and then given up, produces a mere semblance of happiness;
but completely renounced, it conduces to supreme bliss (<s>paramānanda</s>). // <s>AppVs</s>_37 //
Excessive wealth is destroyed by the king or by the thief;

children.text: anne khalvatimukte vamanaṃ vā syādvireko vā || 38 ||
children.translated_text: indeed, when too much food is taken, there is either vomiting or purging. // <s>AppVs</s>_38 //
He bows, he flatters, he prostrates, he constantly roams about —
as if possessed by a demoness (<s>piśācī</s>), the man who has fallen under the sway of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). // <s>AppVs</s>_39 //
Parents are [acquired] from the unseen [<s>adṛṣṭa</s>] of birth; sons and sons-in-law also from the unseen [<s>adṛṣṭa</s>];
relatives from the unseen [<s>adṛṣṭa</s>] of quarrel — when [all] this is established, what is to be desired? // <s>AppVs</s>_40 //
What one daily performs for the other world of one's own father —
let this be taken as an illustration: is it not sufficient for dispassion toward sons? // <s>AppVs</s>_41 //
When poverty does not follow [a person, even into death], what sign has been seen that follows?
If the non-fulfillment of desire [is the definition of poverty], then the world is wretched from [the creator] <s>Brahmā</s> down. // <s>AppVs</s>_42 //

children.text: na khalu dhanatvaṃ jātiryasya yadiṣṭaṃ tadeva tasya dhanam /
children.translated_text: Wealth is not determined by birth; whatever is desired by someone — that itself is his wealth;
that very thing is [wealth] for the vulgar, but for the wise, possessionlessness (<s>ākiṃcanya</s>) is wealth. // <s>AppVs</s>_43 //
If craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is accepted, the entire world must also be accepted;

children.text: svīkriyate yadi śāntiḥ svātmāpi svasya bhavati na vā || 44 ||
children.translated_text: if peace (<s>śānti</s>) is accepted, even one's own self may or may not be one's own. // <s>AppVs</s>_44 //
That [inner state] which subdues the giver, which appeases his retinue,
which feels no shame inwardly — the attainment of [that] disposition, to what is it comparable? // <s>AppVs</s>_45 //
To fill a belly merely a span in size, how great is the effort required?
To drink water with a handful, must one dig a reservoir as well? // <s>AppVs</s>_46 //
Bodily beauty clearly [lasts] half a watch without adornment, and two watches without food —
yet how deeply deluded are those who are fixated even upon this! // <s>AppVs</s>_47 //
They call a young woman 'barren'; they abandon a mother of many sons, [calling her] 'old';
they reproach one with few sons — what wife is pleasing to the heart of a lustful man? // <s>AppVs</s>_48 //

children.text: yānti śucamakṛtadārā dve bhārye neti kṛtadārāḥ /
children.translated_text: The unmarried grieve 'no wife'; the married [grieve] 'not two wives';
they [say] 'not another man's wife' — we do not see a man satisfied with women. // <s>AppVs</s>_49 //
In carrying out the orders of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), I consider this entire world to be of one nature;

children.text: tiryañca iti narā iti devā ityanyato bhedaḥ || 50 ||
children.translated_text: the distinction 'these are animals,' 'these are humans,' 'these are gods' comes from elsewhere [i.e., is irrelevant]. // <s>AppVs</s>_50 //
The site for the release of semen is something like the place for the evacuation of excrement and urine —

children.text: striya iti vihitaṃ vidhinā kiyadatra janā nimajjanti || 51 ||
children.translated_text: such has been ordained by the Creator with respect to women; how deeply people plunge into this! // <s>AppVs</s>_51 //
Having studied the <s>Vedas</s> according to rule, having investigated their meaning through <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>,

children.text: dārāḥ kartavyā iti kenedaṃ prahasanaṃ kathitam || 52 ||
children.translated_text: [the conclusion is:] 'one must take a wife' — who has composed this farce? // <s>AppVs</s>_52 //
With difficulty they are earned, daily they must be maintained and pampered —
these perverse women, enjoyed by the deluded, [yield only] defective pleasure. // <s>AppVs</s>_53 //

children.text: aśnīta pibata svādata jāgrata saṃviśata tiṣṭhata vā /
children.translated_text: Eat, drink, enjoy, stay awake, lie down, or stand —
but think, even once a day, that this bondage to the body is excessive! || 54 ||

children.text: kiṃ vijitayā pṛthivyā kiṃ kāñcanabhūbhṛtā karasthena /
children.translated_text: What use is the conquered earth? What use is a golden mountain in one's hand?
What use are celestial women, when death has been inscribed by <s>Brahmā</s>? || 55 ||
Life lasts but a few moments — as if one has studied a few scriptures in a few breaths,
so long does [life] disturb, and weave new entanglements! || 56 ||

children.text: svalpo jīvanakālaḥ svalpā dhīḥ paricayaḥ svalpaḥ /
children.translated_text: The span of life is short, the intellect is limited, experience is meager —
yet even so, we might somehow cross over, if only new scriptures did not keep arising! || 57 ||

children.text: kuta āgataṃ na jāne kva nu vā gantavyamidamapi na jāne /
children.translated_text: Whence I have come, I do not know; where I must go, this too I do not know.
Where are you wandering now, on the great path of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), in deep darkness? || 58 ||
Enveloped in darkness, wandering, they perceive objects neither near nor far;

children.text: avayanti tu vispaṣṭaṃ taḍitābhihate śirasi mūḍhāḥ || 59 ||
children.translated_text: but the deluded see clearly [only] when lightning strikes upon their heads! || 59 ||
Here young women blink; there [in heaven] young women do not blink —

children.text: īdṛkṣo hi viśeṣaḥ svargaḥ svarga iti kiṃ tatra || 60 ||
children.translated_text: if such is the distinction, then what of it? 'Heaven is heaven' — what is there [really]? || 60 ||

children.text: kopo maitrāvaruṇeḥ śāpo vā tārkikasya muneḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether it be the anger of <s>Maitrāvaruṇi</s> (Agastya) or the curse of the logician-sage,
if one remembers [the Lord] even once — let the position of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) not be [desired], even for an enemy! || 61 ||
Let one go to <s>Amarāvatī</s> (Indra's city), or let one go to the city of <s>Caturānana</s> (Brahmā) —

children.text: punarāgantavyaṃ yadi puṃsā kiṃ sādhitaṃ bhavati || 62 ||
children.translated_text: if one must return again, what has a person accomplished? || 62 ||

children.text: bhuktā bahavo dārā labdhāḥ putrāśca pautrāśca /
children.translated_text: Many wives have been enjoyed, sons and grandsons have been obtained,

children.text: nītaṃ śatamapyāyuḥ satyaṃ vada martumasti manaḥ || 63 ||
children.translated_text: even a hundred years of life have been lived — tell the truth: is there a desire to die? || 63 ||
Seeing that sense objects are by nature subject to separation, who would feel possessiveness?
Who would buy with wealth a horse that has reached the state of perishing? || 64 ||
In the absence of food there is death; food comes from rice, rice from rain,
rain from <s>tapas</s> (austerity) — thus declaring, one performs <s>tapas</s> for the sake of death [i.e., mere survival]! || 65 ||

children.text: kiṃ na nigṛhṇanti manaḥ kiṃ na bhajante janāḥ śivaṃ śaraṇam /
children.translated_text: Why do people not restrain the mind? Why do they not take refuge in <s>Śiva</s>?
Merely through the difference of intention, in the very means of liberation, they are not bound! || 66 ||
This body is for enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) for the base, and for union (<s>yoga</s>) for the discerning.

children.text: bhogāya ca yogāya ca na kalpate durvidagdhānām || 67 ||
children.translated_text: For those who are perversely clever, it serves neither enjoyment nor union! || 67 ||
When the sage says '<s>brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>caṇḍālas</s>' — referring to the great travelers,
this was spoken with reference to the great travelers on the path of worldly existence (<s>bhavamārga</s>)! || 68 ||

children.text: ekadvāḥ kṣitipatiṣu dvitrā deveṣu pañcaṣā druhiṇe /
children.translated_text: One or two among earthly kings, two or three among the gods, five or six in <s>Druhiṇa</s> (Brahmā) —
only these many in the world are drops of the ocean of <s>Brahmānanda</s> (the bliss of Brahman)! || 69 ||
When knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>) is concealed by ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), what can action (<s>karma</s>) accomplish?

children.text: vikale cakṣuṣi tamasā vyādāya mukhaṃ kimīkṣeta || 70 ||
children.translated_text: When the eye is impaired by darkness, even with mouth wide open, what can one see? || 70 ||
Extremely turbid, quickly vanishing, appearing for but a moment, producing no [lasting] desire —
how can people rejoice by clinging to the firefly of [mere worldly] knowledge? || 71 ||

children.text: ayutaṃ niyutaṃ vāpi pradiśantu prākṛtāya bhogāya /
children.translated_text: Let them bestow ten thousand or a million for ordinary worldly enjoyment —
the deluded will not purchase <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation) with even five or six bilva leaves! || 72 ||
As long indeed as they strive [for worldly things], so long a knot is tied in the noose.

children.text: nibhṛtaṃ yadi vartante kālena sraṃsate pāśaḥ || 73 ||
children.translated_text: If they remain still, in time the noose falls away! || 73 ||
The sages restrain their breaths, they neither eat nor drink,

children.text: stūyante sujanaiḥ kiṃ kaṇṭhe kurvanti kanakapāśamime || 74 ||
children.translated_text: and are praised by good people — [yet] do these [worldly folk] bind a golden noose around their throats? || 74 ||
People gladly smile at the occasion of describing the delights of <s>Kailāsa</s>,
but at the occasion of describing the means [of attaining it], they turn their faces away! || 75 ||
'How is <s>Vaṅga</s>? How is <s>Aṅga</s>?' — one inquires idly about countries,
but no one in the world desires to know 'What is the city of <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death) like?' || 76 ||
The sense of 'mine' (<s>mamakāra</s>) should be abandoned. If it cannot be abandoned,

children.text: kartavyo mamakāraḥ kiṃ tu sa sarvatra kartavyaḥ || 77 ||
children.translated_text: then let possessiveness be cultivated — but it should be cultivated toward everything [i.e., toward the universal Self]! || 77 ||

children.text: putrā iti dārā iti poṣyānmūrkho janānbrūte /
children.translated_text: 'These are my sons,' 'these are my wives' — the fool speaks of people as his dependents,

children.text: andhe tamasi nimajjannātmā poṣya iti nāvaiti || 78 ||
children.translated_text: sinking in blind darkness, he does not realize that the Self (<s>ātman</s>) is the [true] dependent! || 78 ||
Whatever was conceived in the womb, and whatever was long contemplated in hell —
all that was wiped away in an instant by contact with the wind of sense objects! || 79 ||
The activity of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), characterized by inhalation and exhalation, whose nature is going out and coming back,

children.text: karṣati manaso vṛttiṃ kulaṭeva kulastriyaṃ mugdhām || 80 ||
children.translated_text: drags the activity of the mind, like an unchaste woman [drags away] a naive woman of good family! || 80 ||
Exceedingly deep, unstained, unshakable, with unseen shore, insurmountable,
dense with unceasing waves — I have beheld the ocean of <s>vijñāna</s> (supreme knowledge) of the great ones! || 81 ||
To remove the terrible [cycle of] worldly existence (<s>bhava</s>), some take refuge in the non-terrible (<s>Aghora</s>, i.e., Śiva).
For those terrified of transmigration, the refuge is the power of <s>Śāmbhavī</s> (Śiva's <s>śakti</s>)! || 82 ||
If the noose is to be released, then <s>Paśupati</s> (the Lord of Bound Souls, i.e., Śiva) alone must be approached.

children.text: na khalu vyatimucyante paśavaḥ pāśena saṃbaddhāḥ || 83 ||
children.translated_text: Animals (<s>paśus</s>, bound souls) bound by the noose are certainly not freed [by themselves]! || 83 ||
Enough, enough with the mothers already experienced! Enough with the fathers too!
If one must exist eternally, let it be as the son of [the true] Mother and Father [i.e., Śiva and Pārvatī]! || 84 ||

children.text: dhanyāste bahudevāḥ svāmini yeṣāṃ na durbhikṣam /
children.translated_text: Blessed are those who worship many gods, for whom there is no famine of masters.

children.text: jātu na jānīmo vayamekaṃ taṃ svāminaṃ pūrṇam || 85 ||
children.translated_text: But we have never known [any master] — [we know] only that one complete Lord! || 85 ||

children.text: santu bṛhanto devāḥ kiṃ tu na tānnantumīhate cetaḥ /
children.translated_text: Let the great gods exist — but the mind does not wish to worship them.
By the logic of [approaching] the wealthy and generous, one should contemplate in the mind only the Conqueror of Death (<s>Antakajit</s>, i.e., Śiva)! || 86 ||

children.text: nidhyāyasi viṣayasukhaṃ na dhyāyasi viṣamamasya paripākam /
children.translated_text: You meditate on the pleasure of sense objects but do not contemplate the terrible ripening of its [consequences]!

children.text: bandhuṃ tameva cintaya baddhuṃ moktuṃ ca yaḥ kṣamate || 87 ||
children.translated_text: Contemplate rather that kinsman [Śiva] who is able both to bind and to release! || 87 ||
The dwelling is the approach to the <s>guru</s>; the refuge is the preparatory practice of the five-syllabled [mantra] (<s>pañcākṣarī</s>);
the wealth is the cessation of desire — for those men dwelling in the final stage of life (<s>antyāśrama</s>)! || 88 ||

children.text: kau pitarau kaḥ putraḥ kaḥ svāmī yaḥ prapañcasya /
children.translated_text: Who are the parents? Who is the son? Who is the master of this manifest world?
When duality has set, what is this and what is that — such questioning [ceases]! || 89 ||

children.text: sa vidhiryatte vidadhati sa pratiṣedho yato nivartante /
children.translated_text: That is the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) from which one proceeds; that is the prohibition (<s>pratiṣedha</s>) from which one turns back.
That is the <s>Upaniṣad</s> which the steadfast ones speak — the <s>Śaivas</s>, who have heard and are [ready to] die [for truth]! || 90 ||
Abandon <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), which is without essence! Take refuge in the Beloved of <s>Pārvatī</s> (Śiva)!
Trust in the crest of the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas) — [then] this entire universe will be at your command! || 91 ||

children.text: bhavyamabhavyaṃ vā naḥ pralikhatu vedhāḥ sudurmedhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Let <s>Vedhā</s> (Brahmā), that dull-witted one, inscribe for us what is auspicious or inauspicious —

children.text: savyamasavyaṃ vā naḥ śaraṇaṃ caraṇaṃ maheśasya || 92 ||
children.translated_text: whether favorable or unfavorable, our refuge is the feet of <s>Maheśa</s> (the Great Lord, Śiva)! || 92 ||

children.text: vedhāḥ kathaṃ hariḥ kathamiti tu praśne vayaṃ mūkāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'How is <s>Vedhā</s> (Brahmā)? How is <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu)?' — to such questions we are mute.
We know <s>Śiva</s> alone; we know none other than <s>Śiva</s>! || 93 ||
Terrible is the forest of sword-leaves; most terrible is the blind darkness [of hell].

children.text: kā vā tataḥ kṣatirnaḥ śaivā vayamā caturvadanāt || 94 ||
children.translated_text: But what harm is there for us from all that? We are <s>Śaivas</s>, [protected] from [the time of] <s>Caturvadana</s> (four-faced Brahmā, i.e., from creation itself)! || 94 ||
Having been initiated in the terrible sacrifice, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, standing at the summit of the family [lineage],

children.text: vidyeśvareṣu kaścana pitāmaho na iti visrambhaḥ || 95 ||
children.translated_text: was a certain grandfather among the lords of knowledge — [there is] no [room for] doubt! || 95 ||
'Let there never be a quarrel!' — thus between <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śivā</s> (Pārvatī), who have attained bodily unity,
a quarrel has arisen for my protection: 'I am [the protector]! I am [the protector]!' || 96 ||
Not for the sake of [heavenly] enjoyments, nor for the sake of [becoming] the basest of men, nor for the sake of other gods —
some few regard [only] the <s>yoga</s> of <s>Māheśvara</s> (the Great Lord, Śiva) as their refuge! || 97 ||

children.text: jñātuṃ hātuṃ viṣayaṃ śrotuṃ mantuṃ gṛhītumātmānam /
children.translated_text: To know, to abandon sense objects, to hear, to contemplate, to grasp the Self (<s>ātman</s>) —

children.text: vatsā yadi na hi ghaṭate tatsādhayatāvimuktāya || 98 ||
children.translated_text: dear ones, if this is not possible [elsewhere], then accomplish it for the sake of <s>Avimuktā</s> (Varanasi, the city never forsaken by Śiva)! || 98 ||

children.text: sāṃkhyaṃ yogaṃ nigamā bhaktiḥ karma pratītiriti /
children.translated_text: <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, the <s>Nigamas</s> (Vedas), <s>Bhakti</s> (devotion), <s>Karma</s> (action), and <s>Pratīti</s> (direct realization) —
all of this is gathered in one place alone: only in <s>Avimuktā</s> (Varanasi)! || 99 ||

children.text: baddhaḥ kaste vakṣyati mukto muktiṃ vijānāti /
children.translated_text: A bound person — who will tell you [the truth]? A liberated one [alone] knows liberation.
If you go to <s>Avimuktā</s> (Varanasi), you will know from the mouth of <s>Viśveśvara</s> (the Lord of the Universe, Śiva) himself! || 100 ||

children.text: na gṛhītaṃ śrutihṛdayaṃ na ca na gṛhītaṃ pariplavaṃ hṛdayam /
children.translated_text: I have not grasped the heart of the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas), nor can I say I have not grasped it — my heart wavers.

children.text: icchāmi ca dhāma paraṃ gacchāmi tu viśvanāthapurīm || 101 ||
children.translated_text: I desire the supreme abode, yet I go to the city of <s>Viśvanātha</s> (Lord of the Universe, Varanasi)! || 101 ||

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Vairāgyaśatakam</s> (Century of Verses on Dispassion), composed by the illustrious <s>Appaya Dīkṣita</s>.
